scope: Teleport devices, consumable teleports, transport access, and charge states
Tools, skill access, quest utility, and light sources

currency.include: Items used as money, exchange units, or a direct currency substitute; include special-mode tokens only when the item has a repeatable exchange or purchase role.
currency.exclude: Ordinary loot, tradeables, keys, tickets, and one-off quest tokens without a currency function.
currency.evidence: Wiki item mechanics or exchange/shop use, with an exact item ID and version/state match.

runes_and_spell_supplies.include: Runes, combination runes, rune containers, and consumable cast supplies whose primary documented use is casting a spell.
runes_and_spell_supplies.exclude: Runecrafting essence materials, essence pouches, talismans/tiaras, and other Runecraft tools remain skill resources/tools or focus items; magic weapons and worn combat gear remain gear.
runes_and_spell_supplies.evidence: Wiki use/effect text establishes spell casting or spell-rune storage. A Runecraft category or the word rune alone does not establish castable spell-supply role.

runecrafting_resources_and_tools.destination: resources/raw-resources for essence; skilling-tools/tools for pouches, talismans, and tiaras
runecrafting_resources_and_tools.include: Rune essence, pure essence, Daeyalt essence, and containers or tools whose role is to support Runecrafting.
runecrafting_resources_and_tools.exclude: Spell runes and rune pouches that store castable runes belong to the spell-supply role.
runecrafting_resources_and_tools.evidence: Use the exact item page to distinguish Runecraft production inputs and essence storage from magic runes used to cast spells. Preserve damaged pouch and capacity states.

teleports_and_transport.include: Consumable teleport scrolls/tablets, rechargeable or degradable teleport devices, charges for a teleport device, teleport containers, and reusable access items whose primary documented effect is transport.
teleports_and_transport.exclude: Quest items with only incidental travel relevance, generic keys, and combat equipment whose travel effect is secondary to its combat role.
teleports_and_transport.evidence: Wiki effect/use text establishes transport and the exact state/charge variant. Variants may share a functional group while keeping distinct IDs and charge counts.

tools_and_skill_access.include: Reusable tools, skill-enabling utility items, gathering/production tools, and task access items primarily used to perform or enable a skill activity.
tools_and_skill_access.exclude: Crafting materials, rewards, or wearable combat gear when evidence shows their primary role is elsewhere. An equippable multi-use item remains gear if its combat or equipment role is substantial.
tools_and_skill_access.evidence: Wiki use/effect text or documented recipe/activity use. Skill name in an item name is insufficient.

light_sources.include: Lit/unlit light-source tools and replaceable-light variants when their function is illumination or environmental access.
light_sources.exclude: Firemaking materials that are consumed to start fires and decorative light-themed cosmetics.
light_sources.evidence: Wiki identifies the item as a light source, describes lighting state, or documents an area mechanic that requires it. Preserve lit, unlit, and charge/fuel states as separate item IDs.

resource_containers.include: Reusable containers that store, carry, gather, or transform resources; include sacks, boxes, bags, barrels, baskets, kits, and containers with inventory contents.
resource_containers.exclude: Ordinary ingredients, empty packaging with no reusable storage role, and containers that are primarily quest/story objects without a practical storage use.
resource_containers.evidence: Wiki capacity/content/withdrawal behavior. Preserve open/closed, charged/uncharged, filled/empty, and size tiers as state variants. Do not merge states based on similar names.

overlap_resolution: Assign the main destination from the item's primary practical role established by Wiki mechanics, not from the current catalog label or name token alone.
Where a resource container holds a currency, rune, or teleport supply, classify the container by storage function and classify its contents by their own role.
Keep Wiki category facets separate from destination: Currency can coexist with a skilling-supply role, and Runecraft is not synonymous with Runes.

Where an item is both wearable/equippable and grants teleport, spell, or skill access, retain the equipment role when equipment utility is substantial; record the secondary use as a note or unresolved overlap instead of forcing a false single-purpose classification.
A direct Wiki item page and exact ID/state evidence outrank inferred family membership. Family analogies may generate review candidates but cannot establish a final classification.
Absence from Wiki category pages, searches, or the current bank fixture is not evidence that an item lacks a function. Mark unavailable or unresolved evidence explicitly.
Quest utility and transport can coexist. Route as transport only when transport is a persistent user-facing function, not merely a quest step.

frequent_use_policy.base_behavior: Do not universally assign frequently-used based on item type, popularity, bank presence, or expected account progression.
frequent_use_policy.user_preference: Allow the player to opt into a configurable set of frequently-used items or families for the main tab. This is a placement preference, not a factual semantic role.
frequent_use_policy.safe_defaults: Only items explicitly configured as staples by the product may receive a default frequent-use placement; preserve their semantic role as currency, rune, teleport, or tool in metadata.
frequent_use_policy.account_limit: Without usage telemetry or player settings, the plugin cannot know how often a specific player uses a tool or teleport. Do not infer individual usage from Wiki data.

confidence_rules.high: Exact-ID Wiki page or structured mechanics match confirms primary function and relevant state.
confidence_rules.medium: Wiki confirms a functional family, but the exact item variant/state is not fully disambiguated.
confidence_rules.low: Classification is inferred from name, icon, similarity, a generic category, or incomplete Wiki evidence. Candidate only; no automatic rule.
confidence_rules.unresolved: Wiki evidence conflicts, is missing, or leaves multi-use priority/state ambiguous. Keep current role pending review and cite the ambiguity.
